alice.song: Heads-up — noticed a regression on canary for long-context traffic. tokens/sec dropped ~25% (320 -> 240) and $/M tokens jumped ~30%. Investigating, but looks tied to attention kernel routing + KV prefetch behavior.

ben.chen: ugh. saw increased kernel launches in the nvprof traces, more memcpy, and a lot more paged-attention hits. sharing quick pprof dump shortly.

carla.ramirez: profiler summary I just pulled from the canary run:
```
Serving profiler snapshot: canary-1972345678
Model: redwood-7b-quant
Workload: mixed seqs (median 1024, tail 2048)
Tokens/sec (baseline): 320
Tokens/sec (canary): 240
Kernel selection breakdown (canary):
  flash_fused_v2: 18%
  paged_attention: 72%
  fused_attn_small: 10%
KV cache hit rate: 62% -> 58% (churn from prefetch)
Prefetch queue flush events: ~4200/min
Observed: increased host<->device memcpy and smaller kernel occupancy per launch
```

alice.song: That matches my surface metrics. The only routing/policy change in that deploy was lowering the KV prefetch hysteresis and prefetch threshold so the runtime prefetches aggressively for mid-length sequences. Config snippet from the deploy: 
```
routing:
  kv_prefetch_threshold: 0.3
  kv_prefetch_hysteresis_ms: 100
```

ben.chen: I think the aggressive prefetch is perturbing the sequence-length distribution seen by kernel selector. Prefetch churn clobbers the KV cache (thrashing) and forces the runtime to route more requests to paged_attention because memory footprint estimates are spikier. Hence more small kernel invocations and lower throughput.

carla.ramirez: Also saw more fallback to paged-attn for sequences that should have used flash_fused_v2. The kernel selector uses an estimated working set and available device memory; prefetch bursts increase estimated pressure.

alice.song: Quick mitigations: 1) revert kv_prefetch_threshold to previous value (0.6) on canary, 2) add metric for prefetch_flush_rate and kernel_mismatch_rate, 3) add unit perf test for mixed-long sequences that asserts no >10% tokens/sec regression.

ben.chen: I can open the rollback PR and add the metric instrumentation. Will also add a temporary guard: if prefetch_flush_rate > 1k/min then disable prefetch for that pod.

carla.ramirez: I'll prototype a change to kernel selector to include prefetch_queue_bytes in the decision vector so we avoid routing to paged-attn if prefetch churn is high. Patch will be low-risk (heuristic only) and feature-gated.

alice.song: Plan sounds good. Owners: ben -> rollback + metrics + canary; carla -> selector heuristic prototype + perf test. Timeline: rollback + canary in next 30m, selector patch in next 24h, follow-up retro.

sre-bot: deploybot: Started rollout of revert-config (user: ben.chen) to canary cluster.

ben.chen: deploybot says rollout in progress. will report back with numbers once stable. :crossed_fingers:

carla.ramirez: for the retrospective, we should also include $/M tokens in the smoke checks for any routing/policy change. this one was cheap to test-on-qa but still slipped into canary since cost checks weren't in the gating path.

alice.song: agreed. adding cost guard to gating checklist.

ben.chen: quick note — command I used to reproduce locally (if you want to perf-run):
```
./perf/run_loadtest.sh --model redwood-7b-quant --seq-dist "mix:40:512,40:1024,20:2048" --concurrency 8 --report tokens_per_sec,kernel_breakdown
```

alice.song: thanks. will validate after canary stabilizes. :eyes:

carla.ramirez: noted for follow-up: run the perf harness with and without prefetch enabled to quantify delta and capture nvprof traces.

ben.chen: back from canary — after revert tokens/sec back to ~318, $/M tokens near baseline. Reverting helped. Opening ticket to track selector change (ENG-PRF-3421).

alice.song: great, closing the immediate alert. leaving ticket for longer-term selector improvements and gating. :thumbsup:

carla.ramirez: thanks team. I'll start the prototype and share PR link in this thread when ready.

ben.chen: +1

alice.song: thanks everyone.
